partial:
\(Hence $\gamma_2^{\alpha} = \Theta(\mathrm{Q})$: it computes quantum query complexity, it does not merely bound it.\) partial Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\gamma_2^{\alpha}(f) = O\big(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon}(f)\big)\)
    LMRSS11 Reichardt11
    Via $\gamma_2^{\alpha} = \Theta(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm})$ above and $\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm} = \Theta(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon})$.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\gamma_2^{\alpha}(f) = \Omega\big(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon}(f)\big)\)
    LMRSS11 Reichardt11

This is the record the function pages appeal to when they enter $\gamma_2 = \Theta(\mathrm{Q})$ rather than computing a factorisation by hand. The interesting reading is the contrast with the positive adversary \(\mathrm{Adv}(f)\): on \(\mathrm{COL}_n\) the positive bound is capped at $O(1)$ by the certificate-complexity barrier while $\gamma_2 = \Theta(n^{1/3})$, so the difference between the two norms is the whole of what sign changes buy.

see also: \(\gamma_2^{\alpha}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Adv}(f)\), \(\mathrm{COL}_n\) data/relations/03-quantum.yaml

partial:
\(The approximate $\gamma_2$ norm *is* the general adversary bound, rewritten as a factorisation norm.\) partial Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\gamma_2^{\alpha}(f) = O\big(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\big)\)
    LMRSS11

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\gamma_2^{\alpha}(f) = \Omega\big(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\big)\)
    LMRSS11

The adversary SDP and the $\gamma_2$ minimisation are two readings of the same optimisation: an adversary matrix $\Gamma$ with $\|\Gamma\|=1$ and small $\|\Gamma\circ\Delta_i\|$ is exactly a small factorisation of the target through the query matrices. Nothing in the translation asks $f$ to be total, so the identification holds verbatim on a promise.

see also: \(\gamma_2^{\alpha}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon}(f)\) data/relations/03-quantum.yaml

lo.note:
A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
